introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, answer all questions): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION II (30 minutes) - DATA ANALYSIS**

In an experiment to investigate how the current, $I$, in a circuit comprising a capacitor and a resistor in series varies with time, $t$, a student obtained the following results.

| Time, $t$ / s | $I$ / $\mu$A |
|---|---|
| 10 | 46.7 |
| 40 | 38.5 |
| 70 | 32.2 |
| 100 | 26.8 |
| 130 | 22.3 |
| 160 | 18.5 |
| 190 | 15.5 |
| 220 | 12.9 |
| 250 | 10.8 |
| 280 | 9.1 |
| 310 | 7.7 |

The current in the circuit is related to the time by the equation $I = I_0\,e^{-t/\beta}$, where $I_0$ and $\beta$ are constants.

Marques imprimées 10 + 8 + 2 = 20, conformes au « Total = 20 marks ». Le sujet imprime « experiment » avec un « x » seul (« xperiment ») et « tim e » : fautes de scan non recopiées.

questions.enonce_markdown: Plot a suitable graph that can be used to determine the values of $I_0$ and $\beta$. *[10 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Choosing the graph.** Take natural logarithms of $I = I_0 e^{-t/\beta}$:
$$\ln I = \ln I_0 - \frac{1}{\beta}\,t$$
This has the form $y = mx + c$ with $y = \ln I$ and $x = t$. So plot **$\ln(I/\mu\mathrm{A})$ (vertical axis) against $t/\mathrm{s}$ (horizontal axis)**: a straight line with **gradient $= -\dfrac{1}{\beta}$** and **intercept on the $\ln I$ axis $= \ln I_0$**.

**Table of values** (to be calculated by the candidate):

| $t$ / s | 10 | 40 | 70 | 100 | 130 | 160 | 190 | 220 | 250 | 280 | 310 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $I$ / $\mu$A | 46.7 | 38.5 | 32.2 | 26.8 | 22.3 | 18.5 | 15.5 | 12.9 | 10.8 | 9.1 | 7.7 |
| $\ln(I/\mu\mathrm{A})$ | 3.84 | 3.65 | 3.47 | 3.29 | 3.11 | 2.92 | 2.74 | 2.56 | 2.38 | 2.21 | 2.04 |

**The graph (to be drawn by the candidate).** Axes labelled $t/\mathrm{s}$ and $\ln(I/\mu\mathrm{A})$; scales that use more than half of each axis, with the horizontal axis starting at $0$ so that the intercept can be read (for example $0$ to $320\ \mathrm{s}$, $20\ \mathrm{s}$ per large square; vertical $2.0$ to $4.0$, or from $0$ with an axis break). All eleven points are plotted accurately; they lie on a straight line of negative gradient, a best-fit line is drawn through them and **extended back to $t = 0$**, where it meets the $\ln I$ axis at about $3.89$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Use your graph to determine the values of $I_0$ and $\beta$. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Gradient.** Take two points far apart on the best-fit line, for example $(10\ \mathrm{s};\ 3.84)$ and $(310\ \mathrm{s};\ 2.04)$:
$$\text{gradient} = \frac{2.04 - 3.84}{310 - 10} = \frac{-1.80}{300} = -6.0\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$$
$$\beta = -\frac{1}{\text{gradient}} = \frac{1}{6.0\times10^{-3}} = 1.7\times10^{2}\ \mathrm{s}\quad(166\ \mathrm{s})$$

**Intercept.** The line cuts the $\ln I$ axis at $t = 0$ at $3.89$:
$$\ln I_0 = 3.89 \;\Rightarrow\; I_0 = e^{3.89} = 49\ \mu\mathrm{A}$$

**$\beta \approx 1.7\times10^{2}\ \mathrm{s}$ (about 166 s) and $I_0 \approx 49\ \mu\mathrm{A}$** (acceptable ranges: $\beta$ from 160 to 170 s, $I_0$ from 48 to 50 $\mu$A). A least-squares fit of the eleven points gives $\beta = 166\ \mathrm{s}$ and $I_0 = 49.0\ \mu\mathrm{A}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the physical significance of $\beta$? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: $\beta$ is the **time constant** of the circuit: the time taken for the current to fall to $1/e$ ($\approx 37\ \%$) of its initial value $I_0$ (at $t = \beta$, $I = I_0/e$). For a capacitor discharging through a resistor, $\beta = RC$. A large $\beta$ means a slow decay of the current. It is related to the half-life of the decay by $t_{1/2} = \beta\ln 2$ (here about $115\ \mathrm{s}$).
